column1: ## Round-4 inputs through `provost --llm` with round4/llm-templates/ (format 1, written by Claude helpers
## from the guide and the input alone), 2026-10-27. Rated once by independent Claude helpers on CRITERIA.md.
## default / multi = round 4's own ratings of the engine (ratings.tsv). filed_by: template | engine | held.

column8: note
column9: format1_limit

column8: Inst/Conf actions, versions, origins, arch and the 0/3/0/1 summary all land in real columns; the two package lists survive but lose their labels (Suggested vs NEW to be installed), so which list is which is gone
column9: Package lists ('Suggested packages:', 'The following NEW packages will be installed:') are a title line plus an indented line of names: the title should become a column; captured the indented lines as a one-column package_lists table and skipped the titles.

column8: Conflict headers, the summary diagnostic and the seven Example lines are right, but every Shift/Reduce derivation tree (most of the input) is dropped, and examples are cut from their conflicts into a separate table
column9: Records span several lines: each conflict warning is followed by its Example line and two derivation trees that belong to it. Captured conflicts and examples as parallel tables (same row order); the derivation trees are skipped.

column8: Conflicts, grammar rules, terminal/nonterminal symbol numbers, items and actions all present with correct values; but items and actions carry no state column, nonterminal on-left/on-right rule lists lose which nonterminal they belong to, grammar lhs blank on | continuation rules
column9: Section titles should become a column: 'State N' names the items/actions under it, and a nonterminal's 'on left:/on right:' lines belong to the symbol line above; also '|' continuation rules inherit the lhs of the row above. Captured each as its own table (states, items, actions, symbols, nonterminal_rules) in file order instead.

column8: Version, file, two failures with durations, error messages, expected/received, frames and counts all present; each failure is split across four unlinked tables, expectations filed wide as Expected/Received/Expected_2/Received_2 in one row, source snippet lines dropped
column9: Records span several lines: a failure is its error line, Expected/Received, the 'at' frame and the '(fail) name [ms]' line, interleaved with echoed source. Captured them as parallel blocks (results, errors, expectations kv with _2 suffixes, frames); source echoes and carets are skipped.

column8: All 17 Environment and Build Metadata fields correct as one wide kv row; the Gemfile section (source line and the No Gemfile.lock found note) and the section headings are dropped
column9: Indented sub-keys belong to the unindented key above (Platforms under Bundler, Gem Home under RubyGems): the hierarchy is flattened into one kv record. The Gemfile/Gemfile.lock echoes at the end are file contents, not data, and are skipped by their DSL keywords.

column8: All 57 AST nodes with kind, address, range, location and detail correct; tree depth/nesting is lost (flattened, no depth column), the two <<<NULL>>> ForStmt children and the Dumping total: header dropped
column9: Tree depth (the |- and `- glyph prefix) is the parent/child structure and cannot be a column; captured one row per node (kind, address, range, location, detail) with the glyphs left out, so the tree is flattened. The trailing attributes vary per node kind and stay in one detail column.

column8: All timer rows and percentages correct, section titles and Total Execution Time lines kept; but timers carry no section column so the six sections (two named identically) are merged, and per-section Total rows are dropped (Miscellaneous section total lost entirely)
column9: Section titles (Pass execution timing report, DWARF Emission, ...) should become a column of the timer rows under them; captured titles and per-section totals as their own tables in section order instead. Timer tables have 3 or 4 time columns depending on the section: two table blocks (with/without System Time). Total rows are skipped.

column8: Records, offsets/fields, sizeof/align, RecordDecls, FieldDecls, bit widths, CGBitFieldInfo and LLVMType all present and correctly named; fields/sizes/bitfields carry no record column, nesting of first/t sub-fields lost, llvm_layout filed as one wide row with _2/_3 suffixes
column9: Records span several lines: each '*** Dumping' dump is a record head line plus its field lines, sizeof/align line, and (IRgen) a Layout block; nested fields are shown by indentation only. Captured records, fields, sizes, decls, ast_fields, bitfields and the LLVMType/IsZeroInitializable kv (with _2/_3 suffixes) as parallel blocks in dump order.

column8: Trace calls split cleanly into file/line/command/args and -- messages kept; the first call (CMakeLists.txt(1) cmake_minimum_required VERSION 3.20, with the help text glued on) is dropped
column9: ok (the one uncovered line is the first trace line with help text glued onto it, a capture artifact).

column8: Version/date, all 11 options with short/long/description and all 34 commands with aliases split out are correct; only the Usage synopsis line (command [options] [arguments]) is dropped, banner is decoration
column9: ok

column8: legend kv row right and all 106 -W flags present in order, but the indentation (parent/child nesting) is dropped: a flat flag list with no depth or parent column, so the tree structure the input exists to show is lost
column9: The tree's nesting (indentation = the parent warning group) cannot be expressed: values are stripped, so the depth is lost and every -W flag becomes one flat row. Legend lines (GREEN = ...) kept as a kv block.

column8: TERM/COLORTERM patterns and the 23 colour entries land as key/color/comment with real names; LINK's two-line comment is cut after the first line, the group comment for the .tar/.tgz archive block and the commented-out #.cmd/#.exe/#.sh entries plus the attribute/colour-code legend are dropped
column9: ok (comment lines, including the one indented continuation of an entry's trailing comment, are skipped; TERM/COLORTERM glob entries are their own table, and the colour entries keep a trailing "# comment" as a column)

column8: summary kv as one wide row with real names (Device..Num._free_extent, 76.5% kept with Free_blocks); histogram as 5 rows with Range_from/Range_to/Free_extents/Free_Blocks/Percent, every value under the right column
column9: ok (the "Extent Size Range" column "32K...   64K-" is split into two columns, Range from / Range to, so the dot leader and dash stay out of the values)

column8: Pattern elts/size, the 50 charset pages (page/bits) and all 42 properties as one wide kv row with real names and correct values; the per-property type/binding markers (s)/(w)/(i)/(f) are stripped from every value, so strong-vs-weak binding is lost
column9: Mostly ok. The charset bitmap rows (hex page: 8 words) belong to the "charset:" property above them and the lone "(s)" line closes that multi-line value; format 1 cannot nest, so they are a separate charset table and the "(s)" terminator is skipped. Quotes and the (s)/(w)/(i)/(f) binding/type annotations are treated as decoration and dropped from values.

column8: Source:util.c, 3 function summaries (called/returned/blocks_executed), 11 branch rows (branch/taken/note/status) and 26 source rows (count/line/source) all present; but branch rows carry no line or function key so which source line each branch belongs to is lost, and source indentation is trimmed
column9: The output interleaves three kinds of rows: "function ..." summaries apply to the source line that follows, and "branch N taken ..." rows belong to the source line above them; format 1 cannot attach them, so they are three flat tables (functions, branches, source) plus a kv block for the line-0 metadata (Source:...). Leading indentation of source text is lost by stripping.

column8: all 13 metric lines kept as metric/percent/of with correct values, and the 5 functions and 2 files listed; but metrics carry no function/file key (association recoverable only by order), 'No calls' for util.c and the Creating lines are dropped, and the final total row is not distinguished
column9: Records span several lines: a "Function 'x'" or "File 'x'" title line followed by its "Lines executed:P% of N" metric lines (and a trailing overall Lines-executed line with no title). The title should be a column of the metric rows; format 1 cannot carry it, so titles and metrics are separate flat tables. "Creating 'x.gcov'" and "No calls" are skipped.

column8: 8 header fields as one row with real names (display_name..unix_mount) and all 48 attributes as one row named standard_type..owner_group; every value under its own key, nothing dropped
column9: ok (two kv blocks: the top-level fields and the indented "attributes:" section; the "attributes:" heading itself is skipped)

column8: WORK, 62 packagefile package/file rows and 13 commands (env/command/args/note with # internal in note) are right; the modinfo line of the importcfg.link heredoc (GOARCH/GOOS/CGO/buildmode) is dropped, and packagefiles do not record which of the two heredocs they came from
column9: Mostly ok. The heredoc structure (which "cat > importcfg << 'EOF'" command owns the following packagefile lines) cannot be expressed, so all packagefile lines from both importcfg files land in one table; the binary "modinfo" blob line inside the second heredoc is skipped. Commands are one table of env / command / args / "# internal" note.

column8: package/import, type Ring struct, the Value field with comment and 8 func signatures split into receiver/func/params/result are correct; but every doc comment is gone: the package sentence, the 4-line Ring description, 'Has unexported fields' and all per-function docs (about 60% of the input), a substantial part missing
column9: Records span several lines: each "func ..."/"type ..." signature is followed by its indented doc paragraph, and struct field lines belong to the "type X struct {" above them; format 1 cannot attach them, so doc prose, section titles (TYPES), closing braces and the package summary are skipped, and signatures, types and struct fields are flat tables.

column8: yaml parser pivots 109 'name: description' records into one 110-column row (linter names as headers, descriptions as values, [fast]/[auto-fix] tags kept inline); the Enabled/Disabled section split is lost so no linter carries its status, and the last record 'wsl [deprecated]' is dropped
column9: Section titles ("Enabled by your configuration linters:" / "Disabled ...") should become an enabled/disabled column of each linter row; format 1 cannot carry a section into rows, so they are skipped and all linters land in one table (with [deprecated] status and trailing [fast, auto-fix] flags as columns).

column8: issues table right (file/line/col/message/linter, 9 rows) and the by-linter summary counts right; the source-code excerpt line under each issue is dropped (carets are decoration), 9-issue total only derivable
column9: Each issue is followed by a source-snippet line and a caret line that belong to the issue above; format 1 cannot attach them, so they are skipped (a negative-lookahead skip drops any line that is not an issue or summary line). Issues and the per-linter counts are tables.

column8: flat profile (4 rows, real headers) and the 5 primary call-graph entries are right; the 8 caller/callee rows carry no parent-entry or caller-vs-callee column so the graph linkage is lost; sample-granularity lines and <spontaneous> dropped; index-by-name section redundant
column9: The call graph groups parent/child lines around each [n] primary line; format 1 cannot tie callers/callees to their entry, so primary lines and caller/callee lines are two flat tables (joinable on index). The "Index by function name" list prints two entries per line, so it is skipped.

column8: source file and terminal name/aliases/description right; the capability list is kept as one comma-joined blob per input line instead of one row per name=value pair, so capabilities are merged, nothing lost
column9: Each capability line holds several comma-separated capabilities (bool, name#num, name=str) and a string value may itself contain commas; format 1 yields one value per group, so each line becomes one row holding its whole comma list.

column8: all 90 log lines land in 7 typed tables (pauses, phases, heap regions, metaspace, cpu, init kv, remaining log) with GC id/uptime per row and real column names; only the init-line uptimes are dropped
column9: ok

column8: class, 8 members (modifiers/type/name/params/throws), descriptors, exception table, line numbers and all 71 bytecode rows present with real names; but bytecode, line-number, exception and descriptor rows carry no method column so which member each belongs to is lost
column9: Members span two lines (declaration, then an indented descriptor line) and bytecode/line-number/exception rows are nested under their method; format 1 cannot attach them, so members and descriptors are parallel tables (row i matches row i) and the bytecode, line-number and exception tables are flat without a method column.

column8: usage, virtual space, waste, header pool, internal stats and settings all right with real names; the 45 chunk-freelist rows and 3 totals have no Non-Class/Class/Both column so the grouping is lost; leading pid 20907 dropped
column9: The chunk-freelist sub-titles (Non-Class / Class / Both) should become a column of the freelist rows and of the "Total word size" rows; format 1 cannot, so they are skipped and the rows of the three lists are concatenated in order (15 sizes each).

column8: all 13 events, every field value and all 6 stack frames present with values under right names; but each event is split across three tables (event name, flat field/value list, frames) with no event id linking them, so records are not one row each; stack '...' dropped
column9: Each event is a multi-line record (`type {` then `key = value` lines, optionally a stack trace) that should become one row per event; format 1 cannot group them, so events, field/value pairs and stack frames are three flat tables in file order.

column8: recording header kv (Version/Chunks/Start/Duration) and all 52 event-type rows with real headers Event_Type/Count/Size_(bytes); nothing lost
column9: ok

column8: process id, JVM version, collector/threads and 12 heap-config rows right with bytes and MB split; heap-usage rows have no space column (G1 Heap/Eden/Survivor/Old) and the 4 percent-used values sit in a separate unlabeled table; 'Debugger attached', 'Server compiler detected', 'thread-local allocation' lines dropped
column9: The Heap Usage section titles (G1 Heap, Eden Space, Survivor Space, G1 Old Generation) should become a column of the usage rows and the "% used" line a column of the same record; format 1 cannot, so titles are skipped, the usage rows are concatenated in order and the percentages are a separate one-column table.

column8: 21 option names and arguments right, but descriptions are mostly empty: only the first line is kept and only when it shares the option line, every continuation line is dropped, and the trailing pattern-list paragraph is lost; a substantial part of the input is missing
column9: Each plugin's description wraps over continuation lines indented to column 28 that belong to the row above; format 1 cannot join them, so the row keeps only the text on the option line (often empty) and the continuation lines and footer prose are skipped.

column8: All 17 Java threads (every header field) and 9 VM threads land one row each with real names, states/frames/monitors complete; but frames and monitors are filed in separate tables with no thread key so stack-to-thread linkage is lost, and the timestamp, JVM version line, SMR thread list and the two "No compile task" lines are dropped.
column9: ok. Stack frames and monitor lines belong to the thread header above them (records span several lines); format 1 flattens them into separate frames/monitors/thread_states tables with no thread column. A truncated header line without a thread name still matches vm_threads (name empty).

column8: Both sections survive as cpus (19 rows) and features (52 rows) with real column names and full descriptions; only the trailing usage prose (+feature/-feature hint) is dropped.
column9: ok. The two sections (CPUs, features) share one line layout; they are told apart by the fixed "Select the X processor." wording llc prints for every CPU, so each section gets its own table.

column8: Executable, breakpoint, process events, threads, backtrace frames, source listing, variables and image list all land in the right columns; but the two struct dumps (p *it, p *it->next) are merged into one 8-row field/value table with no record key and their types "(const item)"/"(item)" dropped, and the lldb command lines and caret marker are not kept.
column9: Interactive session: (lldb) command prompts are skipped, so each output block cannot name the command that produced it; struct members from several `p` commands land in one struct_fields table (the "(type) {" opener is skipped); source listing rows keep the -> marker as a column.

column8: File line, compile-unit header (all 8 fields) and all 37 DIEs (offset+tag) and 124 attributes are present under real names; but the attributes table carries no DIE offset so attributes are detached from their DIE (linkable only by order) and the DIE nesting depth is lost.
column9: DIEs span several lines (an offset+tag header plus indented DW_AT_ attribute lines) and the tag indent encodes tree depth: format 1 cannot attach attributes to their DIE or express depth, so dies and attributes are two flat tables.

column8: Summary kv (8 fields), instruction-info table with real headers and MayStore mark in the right column, legend and 14 resources are all correct; but both resource-pressure tables are collapsed to a single "pressures" string per row instead of the 14 [0]..[13] columns.
column9: Resource-pressure tables have one column per resource unit ([0]..[N], count varies by CPU), which named groups cannot express: each pressure row is kept as one "pressures" value plus the instruction. Instruction Info uses fixed-width 7-char cells (MayLoad/MayStore/HasSideEffects are blank or *), matched by width.

column8: File kv, ELF header (19 fields incl. Ident) all present under real names; but the 7 sections are filed as a 70-row field/value list rather than one row per section, and their Flags values and SHF_* bits sit in separate tables with no section key.
column9: Nested brace tree (ElfHeader{Ident{}} and Sections[Section{}]): format 1 cannot nest, so top-level and ElfHeader fields are kv blocks and the repeated Section fields become a flat field/value table (no section index column); Flags [ (0x..) ] openers and their bit lines are separate tables.

column8: Entering-directory, the 4 build steps (step/total/action), the metrics table with real headers (count, avg (us), total (ms)) and the hash-load line (load/entries/buckets) all land correctly; nothing dropped.
column9: ok

column8: All 15 GC events parse into 17 real named columns (pid, isolate, time, before/after MB, durations, mu, reason) with correct values; but the interleaved "kept 2667" line is dropped (coverage 93%).
column9: ok. "kept 2667" is the traced program's own stdout, not a GC line: left uncovered rather than matched by a value-specific skip.

column8: All 47 ops land one per row with seq, class, op, flags and next correctly split, and the syntax-check line is kept; but the tree indentation depth (the optree structure) is lost and the "syntax OK" status is reduced to the file name.
column9: ok. The op indentation encodes tree depth (parent/child), which a flat table cannot express; the columns are seq, class, op, flags, next.

column8: All 18 measurement rows parse with method, ops/sec and usecs/op correct (n/a handled); but the five section headings are dropped so the one-8kB-write and two-8kB-write groups (identical method names) are indistinguishable, and the preamble lines (1 second per test, O_DIRECT supported) are lost.
column9: Section titles ("Compare file sync methods using one 8kB write:" etc.) should become a column of the sync_methods table; format 1 cannot carry a section title into rows, so all unindented prose/title lines are skipped and the rows from every section go into one table.

column8: histogram table with real names (us, %_of_total, count) and all 15 rows; the two preamble lines filed as a kv summary row (2 seconds, 34.52 ns); nothing lost
column9: ok

column8: class, section counts, 7 methods with modifiers, 5 parameters and 6 returns all captured with real names; but parameters and returns are filed as separate tables with no method column, so which method owns each parameter/return is lost (only recoverable by order, and ambiguous since __construct has no return)
column9: Nested structure (class > sections > methods > parameters/return) cannot be expressed: each level is its own flat table, so parameters and returns are not tied to their method; "- Parameters [N] {" openers and closing braces are skipped.

column8: each diagnostic one row with level, message, line, file split correctly; the "has 5 pod syntax errors" summary kept as file/errors row; nothing lost
column9: ok

column8: headerless 9-column TSV read as 80 rows under meaningful names (name, context, category, vartype, default, min, max, short_desc, long_desc); every value under the right column, empty min/max/long_desc preserved as blanks
column9: ok (tab-separated, 9 fixed fields; empty cells kept as empty groups)

column8: first line consumed as the header ("Process:_sleep", "State:_S_(sleeping)", "C"), so every later line sits under wrong column names; key: value pairs never split (CPU#, PID, Vsize, RSS, Nice etc. remain raw text), section headings become data rows
column9: Two or three "Key: value" pairs per line; a kv block takes one pair per line, so each multi-pair line layout is its own one-row table block with a group per key, and single-pair lines go to one kv block. Section titles (Memory, Scheduling, ...) carry no data and are skipped rather than becoming a column.

column8: indent-tree keeps every line with its section (NAME, DESCRIPTION, FUNCTIONS, DATA, FILE) as parent and real values (functions one per row, FILE path); but prose paragraphs are split one row per line and the rgb_to_abc/abc_to_rgb lines are parented to a sentence rather than DESCRIPTION; no column separates section heading from text
column9: Section titles (NAME, FUNCTIONS, DATA, ...) should become a column; instead each section kind is its own block. Free-prose DESCRIPTION lines and the pydoc boilerplate cannot be data: the fixed boilerplate is skipped, module-specific prose stays uncovered (84%); "Key: value" prose lines go to a generic kv block.

column8: all 18 formatters captured, aliases kept, description and (filenames ...) correctly split; but aliases and descriptions are two tables linked only by row order where one table was wanted, and the Pygments version line is dropped
column9: Records span two lines (a "* aliases:" line plus an indented description line); format 1 cannot join them, so aliases and descriptions are two parallel tables in the same row order.

column8: session kv, progress line, all 7 short-summary results with outcome/test/message, totals and duration, the failing source/E lines, location, and the captured log line are all right; but the captured stdout text ("checking half-up rounding", "net 100 -> de") is lost (captured table carries only stream/phase, no content) and no table ties captures/errors to their test
column9: The failure detail (source context, E lines, location, captured output) belongs to the test-section header above it; format 1 cannot nest, so each kind of line is its own flat table. Captured stdout lines are free text and stay uncovered (94%).

column8: every line kept, field names / node types / values correctly split into field, node, value columns; but the nesting is flattened with no depth or parent column, so the tree structure (which node owns which field) cannot be rebuilt from the output
column9: Nesting depth (indentation) and which node a field belongs to cannot be expressed; one row per line with field / node (opened on this line) / value, closing brackets left as decoration.

column8: all 5 frames (file, line, function), 5 source lines and 3 exceptions captured with real names and correct values; but the three tables are linked only by order, frames are not attributed to their traceback/exception, and the chaining lines ("direct cause of", "During handling of") are dropped
column9: Frames, source lines and exceptions of one traceback belong together and the chain has three tracebacks; format 1 cannot group them, so they are three flat tables in document order; the chaining sentences and caret lines are skipped.

column8: all 55 opcodes as one row each with pos/code/opcode/arg intact, summary line kept as field/value; only the nesting indentation (stack depth) is not carried as a column
column9: ok. The indent before the opcode name (MARK nesting depth) is not a column; pos/code/opcode/arg are.

column8: every class and def is one row with kind/name/bases/lineno correct and in input order; the class-to-method nesting is only implicit in row order (no parent column), bases column empty for defs as in input
column9: records span several lines: a class line plus indented def lines that belong to it; format 1 cannot attach methods to their class. Did one table in document order with a kind column (class/def) so the grouping can be read back from row order.

column8: all 5 warnings land with file/line/category/message correct and the tracemalloc note is kept, but each warning record is split across two tables: the offending source line sits in a separate source dataset linked only by row order
column9: a warning spans two lines: the location/category/message line plus an indented source line that belongs to it. Put the source lines in a second table in the same order; the stray "ResourceWarning: Enable tracemalloc..." line is a kv record.

column8: header names applied (File_Name/Modified/Size), all 6 entries one row each, names with spaces and UTF-8 kept intact, sizes under Size
column9: ok (fixed-width columns with spaces inside File Name: the name is anchored on the timestamp that follows it).

column8: all five sections survive: 13 progress rows with progress/type/key/size, 6 biggest-per-type rows, sampled count, total key length + avg len, and the 6 per-type stats rows (keys/type/total/pct/avg); only the leading comment banner is dropped
column9: ok. The two summary sentences (Sampled N keys, Total key length) are one-row tables rather than one summary record.

column8: second header row applied (keys/mem/clients/blocked/requests/connections), all 7 samples one row each with values under the right column; group banner (data/load/child) reduced to an empty child column
column9: ok (requests keeps its delta, "4652 (+0)", as one value; the empty child column is optional).

column8: all 6 iseq headers and all 35 instructions land with offset/insn/operands/line/events correct and the two local-table size/argc lines are parsed, but instructions and local tables carry no iseq column (offsets restart at 0000 with no link to their disasm block) and the local-variable name lines ([ 3] name@0<Arg> ...) are dropped
column9: section titles (== disasm: #<ISeq:name@file:line ...>) should become a column of the instruction rows; put them in their own table in order instead. Local-variable lines ("[ 3] name@0<Arg>[ 2] qty@1 ...") hold a variable number of entries per line: skipped.

column8: every setting is present under its real name (speed/rows/columns/line, each control char, each mode flag incl. cs8 under csize and nl0 under nldly) but the single terminal record is split across 3 control_chars rows and 6 modes rows, one per input line, with empty cells elsewhere; an unused flush column was invented
column9: several "key = value" pairs and several mode flags per line, wrapped at terminal width; one record should hold all of them. Used fixed-order optional groups so each wrapped line becomes a sparse row with the right columns whatever the wrap points.

column8: all 8 groups, their descriptions and all 53 syscalls are present under group/description/syscall, but each group record is split across rows: the group name, its comment and each syscall sit on separate rows with the other columns empty, so a syscall row does not carry its group
column9: section titles (@group) and their comment should become columns of the syscall rows. Used one table with sparse group/description/syscall columns in document order so the grouping can be read back.

column8: all 6 [EXTENDED] rows land with status/file/other_file correct (arrow treated as separator) and the "6 overridden configuration files found" summary kept as its own dataset
column9: ok. The unified diff systemd-delta prints after [OVERRIDDEN] entries goes to skip.

column8: all 56 option/value lines as one row each under real names option/value; long quoted format strings and indexed names (status-format[0], update-environment[n]) intact; nothing dropped
column9: ok (option/value table rather than one 56-key kv record: indexed options like update-environment[N] are a list; quotes are kept as tmux prints them)

column8: races, conflicts, thread announcements, locks, 30 stack frames, data-symbol lines and ERROR SUMMARY all extracted under real names with nothing mis-filed, but the 7 tables carry no race/stack key so frames and locks cannot be tied back to the race or thread they belong to (records split across tables), and the Command: ./race / Valgrind-3.22.0 preamble and the program output line 2000 are dropped
column9: records span several lines: each race report is a header line, a 'Locks held' line and an indented stack; format 1 cannot link frames or locks to their race or thread, so each line type is its own table (races, conflicts, threads, locks, frames, symbols) plus the ERROR SUMMARY kv; program stdout (lines without the ==pid== prefix) is skipped.

column8: all 24 timing lines as one row each; header names clock / self+sourced / self applied correctly, with self+sourced blank on the two-number lines and the third number kept under self for sourcing lines; event text intact; only the unit banner dropped
column9: ok (two row layouts, 2 or 3 numbers before the colon, folded into one table with an optional self+sourced column)

column8: document kv, the x namespace, all 30 node lines and all 18 content values are present under real names, but the tree is flattened: nodes carry no depth/parent column, content is split into a separate table with no node key, and the namespace is detached from its element, so the nesting that the indentation encodes (which attribute/text belongs to which element) is lost
column9: tree: indentation encodes nesting and each content= line belongs to the node above it; format 1 cannot express depth or parent, so nodes, content lines, namespaces and the DOCUMENT properties are separate flat blocks.

column8: all 105 lines as one row each with offset / field / raw value / decoded text correctly separated, including the offset-less [Bits 1-2] sub-line, the empty PAYLOAD, the UTF-8 filename and the truncated 5th header; only the indentation of extra-field sub-lines is not recorded (parent row immediately precedes them)
column9: records are groups: each LOCAL HEADER starts a record and indented Length/Flags/... rows belong to the Extra ID above; format 1 flattens all to one offset/field/value/decoded table (the header row and sub-field nesting are not linked).

column8: header applied verbatim (IDENTIFIER TIMESTAMP T C RESOURCE_NAME DESCRIPTION); all 11 events one row each; multi-word descriptions kept whole
column9: ok

column8: all 28 attributes one row each under attribute / value / description / user_settable (input has no header); multi-word descriptions whole, blank location value kept empty, True+ flags intact
column9: ok (no header printed; empty value column handled by requiring 2+ spaces between value and description; columns named as lsattr -H would print them)

column8: all 38 key: value lines kept as one wide row with the keys as column names (END APC -> END_APC); values with embedded colons/spaces (VERSION, FIRMWARE, timestamps) intact, trailing whitespace trimmed
column9: ok

column8: all 12 MAC rows under the real header Vlan / Mac_Address / Type / Ports plus the Total Mac Addresses: 12 summary as a second table; only the prompt, title banner and rule lines dropped
column9: ok
